name: Gray-Scott Turing
desc: A living Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion field where two chemicals react into spots, coral, fingerprint mazes and self-replicating mitosis blobs, forever growing and dividing as feed/kill march a ring of regimes over minutes; rendered as a vivid teal-to-hot-pink coral ramp, an x-ray bone radiograph, blackbody thermal, mossy terrarium, or black fingerprint ink on cream.

energy.doc: contrast / color gain of the V-concentration ramp (higher = hotter, more saturated crests)

scale.doc: display zoom — magnify a sub-region of the pattern (guaranteed visible change)

speed.doc: simulation steps/frame + regime-march rate (0.2 still steps every frame)

density.doc: perpetual V-injector count & radius (nucleation that keeps the field alive & evolving)

feed.doc: Gray-Scott feed offset — shifts the whole regime ring warmer (fuller/coral) or leaner (sparser/spots)

kill.doc: Gray-Scott kill offset — lower = fuller maze, higher = sparser spots (ring stays alive at both extremes)

hue.doc: tint of the breathing glow overlay (does not recolor the raw field ramp)

style.doc: field->color philosophy: coral = vivid teal->cyan->yellow->hot-pink / bone = x-ray white-on-navy radiograph (abstract) / thermal = blackbody ironbow heat / moss = green-ochre terrarium / ink-maze = black fingerprint ink on cream paper (mono, abstract)

seed.doc: deterministic seed-patch layout (rebuilds the field on change)

alpha.doc: opacity for VJ compositing (100 = opaque bg; lower = translucent field via tint)
